blogs.title: Steering Stable Diffusion by Rotating Neurons: A Gentle Introduction to Orthogonal Finetuning
blogs.description: A plain-language tour of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT): why rotating a model’s internal directions (without stretching them) can control what it generates. Covers the big idea, the phase-vs-magnitude intuition from signal processing, and how OFT preserves a model’s original skills while adding new ones.

blogs.title: Angles, Not Magnitudes: How Hyperspherical Energy Preserves Visual Semantics
blogs.description: Explains why the angle between neurons matters more than their size, and introduces hyperspherical energy as a way to keep a pretrained model’s semantic structure intact. Uses visual analogies and simple examples to show how preserving pairwise neuron angles protects image quality and diversity during finetuning.

blogs.title: OFT vs LoRA vs ControlNet: What to Use for Fast, Stable Text-to-Image Control
blogs.description: Compares three popular approaches to controlling diffusion models. Breaks down parameter efficiency, training speed, controllability, and inference overhead. Highlights where OFT shines (no added test-time cost, faster convergence, fewer parameters) and when LoRA or ControlNet might still be useful.

blogs.title: Constrained OFT (COFT): Turning a Powerful Idea into a Reliable Tool
blogs.description: Shows how adding a small-radius constraint around the pretrained model makes finetuning even more stable. Explains the role of the epsilon hyperparameter in balancing flexibility and safety, and offers practical tips for choosing it so you can set-and-forget training schedules.

blogs.title: Personalizing Generators Without Breaking Them: OFT for Subject-Driven Generation
blogs.description: A practical guide to using OFT as a drop-in alternative to DreamBooth-style finetuning. Walks through using just a few subject photos to generate new scenes, and explains why OFT preserves identity better, converges faster, and is less sensitive to finetuning length.

blogs.title: From Edges, Segments, and Landmarks to Pictures: OFT for Controllable Generation
blogs.description: Explains how OFT enables accurate, high-fidelity image control from signals like Canny edges, segmentation maps, or face landmarks. Introduces the paper’s “control consistency” metric (how well the output matches the input control) and summarizes results showing stronger control with fewer parameters.

blogs.title: Under the Hood: The Cayley Trick and Block-Diagonal Orthogonality Made Simple
blogs.description: Demystifies the math powering OFT. Explains the Cayley transform for building orthogonal matrices without heavy computation, and why block-diagonal parameterization keeps OFT lightweight. Includes intuitive diagrams and rules of thumb for setting block sizes and sharing blocks.

blogs.title: Why OFT Converges Faster: Training on a Smooth Sphere
blogs.description: Explores the optimization story behind OFT: finetuning directions on a smooth hypersphere leads to better-behaved training. Connects this to empirical findings in the paper (fewer epochs, less data) and what it means for real-world iteration cycles.

blogs.title: Scaling Up Without Slowing Down: OFT’s No-Overhead Inference
blogs.description: Highlights a practical win: once trained, OFT folds its learned rotation into the original weights, so inference is as fast and light as the base model. Explains why this matters for deployment, cost, and on-device generation.

blogs.title: Composable Skills for Generative Models: The Future of Orthogonal Finetuning
blogs.description: Looks ahead at an exciting possibility: combining multiple OFT matrices (for different skills or styles) by simply multiplying them—while staying orthogonal. Discusses what composable control could unlock, plus open challenges like speeding up training inverses and improving parameter efficiency.
